name: Titan Company Ltd
title: Titan Company Ltd - 500114 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Titan Q4 FY26 demand strong (buyer growth back to 8% from flat), but margins under pressure from gold-price mix and Damas/Middle East losses; management gave a 15-20% 3-5 year CAGR but no FY27 guidance.

summary.headline: Titan Q4 FY26: management guides 15-20% jewellery growth as a 3-5 year CAGR, not FY27; buyer growth returned to 8% and Damas/Middle East losses weighed on Q4.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 top-line growth as its best in the recent past, with all businesses growing. Jewellery buyer growth recovered to 8% in Q4 after being roughly flat for the prior nine months, helped by wedding buying, gold price-led urgency, the exchange campaign and the Festival of Diamonds activation. Profitability was pressured by a ₹82 crore loss at the international subsidiary (largely Middle East, incl. Damas), a ~₹80 crore transfer-pricing adjustment in standalone books, and a ~₹100-120 crore employee special reward booked in unallocated costs in Q4. Management declined to give FY27 numerical guidance and deferred margin outlook to an investor day in the first week of June 2026.

financial_highlights.change: vs flattish for prior nine months
analog ~16%, smart watches declined in units
international business profitable at full-year operating level
vs ₹20-30 crore normally; includes ₹100-120 crore special reward
revenue scale the largest factor; FY26 margin nearly 10%
management says 10-20 bps being lost on gold price mix

financial_highlights.metric: Market share gain (Jewellery, FY26 vs FY25)

segments.name: Jewellery (Tanishq, Mia, Zoya etc.)
segments.commentary: Buyer growth 8% in Q4 vs flat prior nine months; management reiterated 15-20% growth ambition as a 3-5 year CAGR. Analyst-cited TMZ domestic EBIT margin of 11-11.5% band; management says gold mix is eroding margin.

segments.name: CaratLane
segments.commentary: Grew 22-23% in FY26 but growth slowed in Q4 due to Oracle Fusion ERP migration disruption in Jan and early Feb, which hit Valentine's demand. Q4 EBIT margin 8.4%; FY26 nearly 10%.

segments.name: Watches
segments.commentary: FY26 overall growth about 14%; analog about 16% and now about 90% of the watches business. Smart watch units declined.

segments.name: International / Damas (GCC)
segments.commentary: Q4 loss of ₹82 crore attributed to March GCC disruption; full-year operating profit achieved. Damas consolidated from January; Damas separately disclosed only from next year. Tanishq converting some Damas stores in GCC.

segments.name: EyeCare
segments.commentary: Revenue growth 16-17% but EBIT margin down YoY on higher marketing spend and a one-off inventory recall of slow-moving stock; 32 closures, 20 net store reduction.

segments.name: TEAL (Titan Engineering, Justech)
segments.commentary: Management said the Justech acquisition performed well in FY26; growth tailwinds cited from India manufacturing, aerospace, defence and China+1.

segments.name: beYon (lab-grown diamonds)
segments.commentary: Two stores currently; target 10-12 stores in 2-3 cities before a national launch; traction described as good but data too limited.

guidance_outlook: Jewellery growth of 15-20% reiterated as a 3-5 year annualised CAGR, explicitly not a quarterly or FY27 number; management expects to do 'a bit better'.
Q1 and Q2 FY27 may benefit from higher gold prices year on year (ticket size tailwind); Q3 and Q4 depend on gold trajectory given already elevated base.
EBIT growth expected to be at least slightly lower than revenue growth given structural gold-price mix impact; no firm margin range given.
Investor Day planned for first week of June 2026 to provide more detail on margins and growth.
Gold loan tenure raised from 180 to 270 days; no cost increase expected near term; gold supply covered for Q1 with gold exchange program as backup.
capex_capacity: beYon: scale to 10-12 stores in 2-3 cities before deciding on national launch; currently 2 stores, with more stores expected in Q1 FY27.
EyeCare: store network revamp ongoing for about 1.5 years; 32 closures in the quarter, net reduction of 20 stores.
Gold exchange programme running since Q3 FY26 with additional short-notice capacity to scale; Tanishq expanding in GCC via Damas store conversions.
demand_pricing: Buyer growth returned to 8% in Q4 from flat prior nine months, driven by pent-up buyers, wedding purchases pulled forward, exchange campaign and Festival of Diamonds studded campaign.
Management says 'preponement' of purchases can keep recurring; FY27 demand depends on gold trajectory and consumer sentiment.
Gold-price-led ticket size inflation (44% and 40% in the last two quarters, per analyst) expected to help Q1 and Q2 FY27.
Competition described as 'business as usual'; organised players gaining share as industry formalises; Titan estimated 50-60 bps market share gain in FY26.
New 'Hues' natural gemstone-in-gold collection launched: about 200 styles, 50% priced between ₹40,000 and ₹2.5 lakh, going up to ₹10 lakh.
Gold metal loan cost around 3%, no increase expected in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold sourcing and cost outlook given DGFT import licence delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is covered for Q1 FY27; gold exchange programme and other contingency plans in place; no increase in gold loan costs expected near term.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ₹140 crore unallocated loss in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly ₹100-120 crore special reward to employees and partners, announced after full-year results; not franchisee payments.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall and is the jewellery margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold-price-driven product mix is the main pressure, costing about 10-20 bps; management would not give assurance on sustainability and will address it at the June investor day.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15-20% growth guidance hold for FY27 given elevated gold prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is a 3-5 year CAGR target, not an FY27 guide; Q1-Q2 may benefit from gold-led ticket size, while Q3-Q4 depend on gold path.

qa_highlights.question: What caused CaratLane's slowdown in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Oracle Fusion ERP migration caused operational issues in January and early February, affecting Valentine's fulfilment; management sees it as a blip based on December and April trends.

qa_highlights.question: Does the transfer pricing adjustment explain the standalone vs consolidated watch and jewellery profit gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: from FY26 international subsidiaries are treated as low-risk distributors with guaranteed minimum profit, creating about ₹80 crore plus-minus in standalone books that nets out on consolidation.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility and trajectory: drives ticket size, product mix, margin and purchase pull-forward; FY27 H2 comparisons get tougher.
Middle East / GCC disruption affecting Damas and Tanishq GCC operations; Damas Q4 loss of ₹82 crore; minority stake economics and eventual buyout (about four years away).
Gold import licensing delays by DGFT and customs slowness.
Margin erosion from gold-mix shift; 10-20 bps already lost; investor day in June 2026 to clarify.
CaratLane ERP migration impact on Q1 FY27 demand; studded demand recovery.
EyeCare margin pressure from marketing spends and inventory write-back; store network revamp.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and buyer momentum and on the 15-20% multi-year ambition, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins and FY27 numbers, deferring specifics to the June investor day. Explanations of one-offs (Damas, transfer pricing, special reward, ERP) were given directly.
key_quotes: We have ended the year with a superlative Quarter 4 top-line growth, perhaps our best-ever in the recent past.

I think this 15% to 20%, whenever we have given, we have never said it for a quarter or for a certain period. It's typically an annualized number and also a kind of a CAGR for the next three, four years, and I would stay with that.
I would not give you a good assurance that this is sustainable.

adds.what: beYon lab-grown diamond stores: 2 open, target 10-12 stores in 2-3 cities before national launch
Tanishq conversion of some Damas stores in GCC (store count not quantified)

growth.why: Jewellery growth of 15-20% reiterated as a 3-5 year CAGR (not FY27 guidance); management expects to do 'a bit better', backed by Q4 buyer growth of 8%, market share gains of 50-60 bps and gold-price ticket-size tailwind in H1 FY27, but no specific capacity or order numbers were given and margin/FY27 numbers are deferred to a June investor day.
